title: 20-week GPU runway and dynamic price test plan
body:
Purpose:
Quick working plan for a 20-week experiment to validate dynamic per-token pricing levers alongside a short-term GPU runway and headcount phasing. This doc combines a compact budgeting sheet, headcount schedule for the next 5 months, and sensitivity testing matrix for price elasticity by segment. Intended audience: Finance, Revenue Ops, Platform Eng, and Head of Hosting Sales.

Summary (TL;DR):
- We have a projected GPU runway of 20 weeks under current committed capacity (mix: 60% reserved, 40% burst/spot).
- Baseline monthly burn (cash + committed GPU leases + payroll allocation) = $3.8M.
- If we implement dynamic price tiers (trialing 3 variants), model predicts 5–22% incremental ARPU for targeted enterprise cohorts with low churn risk.
- Key risk: enterprise contract churn from perceived price complexity; mitigation: clear communication + temporary credits.

Assumptions and inputs (working):
- Starting runway date: 2026-11-01.
- Committed GPU monthly cost (net of bulk discounts): $1.45M.
- Spot/burst monthly expected cost: $450k (variable).
- Payroll allocation to inference ops + SRE + infra finance: $900k/month.
- Other opex (data egress, storage, licenses): $1.0M/month.
- Monthly revenue baseline (hosted API + Dedicated min): $5.2M.
- Token mix: 65% generation, 35% embeddings/rerank (affects cost per unit).
- Elasticity estimates (initial): enterprise -0.25, mid-market -0.8, self-serve -1.5 (these are placeholders for the experiment).

Budget snapshot (20-week horizon, aggregated to months):
- Month 0 (Nov 2026): Revenue $5.2M | Fixed cost $2.35M | Variable cost $1.2M | Payroll $0.9M | Net cash flow $-1.45M (note: includes one-time tax/prepay adjustments)
- Month 1: Revenue $5.3M | Total cost $3.6M | Net +$1.7M
- Month 2: Revenue (projected w/ price tier B) $5.6M | Total cost $3.65M | Net +$1.95M
- Month 3: Revenue (ramp + pricing tier C to pilot accounts) $5.85M | Total cost $3.7M | Net +$2.15M
- Month 4: Revenue $6.0M | Total cost $3.75M | Net +$2.25M
Notes: the month 0 negative figure reflects quarter-end accruals; cash runway measured excluding contractually committed deferred revenue.

Headcount phasing (5-month plan, hires vs contractors):
- Week 0-8: hire 1 infra SRE (full-time), onboard 2 contractor infra engineers for burst capacity (12-week contracts).
- Week 4-12: hire 1 senior platform finance analyst (to automate per-route chargebacks).
- Week 8-20: evaluate growth-hire for Customer Success (+1 AE) if revenue signal >10% uplift.
- Contingency: freeze non-essential hiring at week 10 if spot-cost-to-revenue ratio > 12%.
Estimated incremental monthly payroll delta (if hires complete): +$46k/month from month 2 onward.

20-week GPU runway calculation (quick sim summary):
- Deterministic: given committed + expected spot, runway to zero cash balance = 19.4 weeks without pricing changes.
- Stochastic Monte Carlo (10k draws; variables: token demand +/-30%, spot cost multiplier 0.6–2.0, enterprise churn probability 0–3%): median runway = 22.1 weeks; 10th percentile = 15.2 weeks.
- Trigger rules: if 10th percentile < 12 weeks -> implement immediate hiring freeze + push non-essential capex.

Pricing sensitivity experiment design (A/B/C variants):
- Control (A): status quo pricing.
- Variant B: introduce a small-step per-token uplift (+7% on generation tokens) for enterprise tier with optional SLA. Offer transitional credit 30 days.
- Variant C: dynamic slab pricing where price per token decreases with committed monthly token bands but base price raised +10% for on-demand burst.

Metrics to track (daily + weekly aggregation):
- Net revenue per 1M tokens by cohort (enterprise, mid-market, self-serve).
- Token throughput by region (NA/EU/APAC) and cost per token computed at infra granularity.
- Churn delta (7/30/90 day) for cohorts in B and C vs control.
- Conversion from trial to paid for any accounts experiencing price uplift (measured as delta in ARR/month).
- SLA-related incident cost and any credits issued.

Sensitivity matrix (quick):
- If enterprise elasticity = -0.25 and uptake of SLA = 18% of enterprises targeted -> expected revenue delta +9%.
- If mid-market elasticity = -0.8 and discounting behavior occurs -> revenue neutral to negative up to -6% without targeted credits.
- If self-serve elasticity = -1.5 -> avoid direct uplift in self-serve; instead use consumption-based nudges and improved packaging.

Communication and commercial controls:
- All enterprise-targeted price changes must be routed through sales + AE notification; 1:1 outreach for top 50 accounts.
- Automated billing preview email 14 days before change.
- Temporary credits (30–60 days) seeded automatically for accounts with >$50k/month spend impacted by price delta.

Engineering/Operational asks (visible tasks):
- Platform: add per-route daily cost calc and token attribution by model variant (ticket JIRA-INF-612). Owner: Priya. ETA 3 weeks.
- Billing: ability to create temporary credit lines programmatically. Owner: Ethan. ETA 2 weeks.
- Observability: create a dashboard with net revenue per 1M tokens by cohort + churn signals. Owner: Liam. ETA 1 week.

Decision gates and go/no-go criteria (end of week 8):
- Go if: net ARPU uplift >6% for targeted enterprise cohort AND no >1.5% absolute increase in 30-day churn.
- No-go if: >2% absolute increase in mid-market churn OR spot-cost run-rate increases >20% above baseline for 3 consecutive weeks.

Open questions / risks (notes for Finance execs):
- We need a clean attribution for revenue uplift where customers simultaneously change product usage; attribution model is non-trivial. Suggest short-term rule: attribute uplift to pricing change for customers in pilot unless usage maps to new features launched concurrently.
- Potential negative PR from perceived "surge pricing" for burst capacity; legal to review messaging.
- Does sales want a rollback path (i.e., stop-gap credits) beyond the automated crediting rule?

Next steps / immediate TODOs (1–2 weeks):
- Finalize cohort list for enterprise pilots (Priya).
- Stand up Monte Carlo rerun after infra accuracy improvements (Sofia -> run with updated spot price distributions).
- Draft customer email template and FAQ for pilot cohorts (Sales + Legal).
- Run tabletop with Support on credit workflows and SLA disputes (week 1).

Appendix A: compact numeric table (for copy to sheet)
- Baseline monthly revenue: 5,200,000
- Baseline monthly committed GPU cost: 1,450,000
- Baseline monthly spot cost estimate: 450,000
- Payroll (allocated): 900,000
- Other opex: 1,000,000
- Net monthly baseline cash flow: 400,000
- Expected uplift month 2 (B variant pilot baseline): +300,000
- Hiring delta monthly (if hires complete): 46,000

Appendix B: Monte Carlo quick notes
- Distribution choices: demand ~ lognormal (mu=0, sigma=0.25), spot multiplier ~ beta-mapped [0.6,2.0], churn ~ binomial with p sampled from Beta(1.5, 80) to concentrate small probabilities.
- Output: produce percentiles (10, 25, 50, 75, 90) and plot to Confluence.

Last note (tone): This is intentionally compact — a working artifact to be expanded into a fuller sheet. I expect iteration after platform instrumentation is in place because our ability to compute cost-per-token by model/route materially changes sensitivity outputs.

Document history:
- 2026-11-02: initial draft (S. Chen)
- 2026-11-10: added Monte Carlo sketch and decision gates (E. Rivera)
- 2026-11-15: updated headcount phasing and trigger thresholds (P. Malhotra)

Questions for reviewers (please annotate in-line):
1) Is the hiring contingency trigger too conservative given current sales pipeline?
2) Are the elasticity priors reasonable or should we widen priors for the Monte Carlo?
3) Any legal/comms concerns with the 30–60 day credit rule?
